Title: Pancakes
Description: These pancakes are soft, golden, and lightly sweet, with a smooth batter that cooks into a tender and comforting dessert. They can be enjoyed plain or customised with delicious additions such as poppy seeds, raisins, vanilla, nuts, or grated apple, making each batch easy to adapt to different tastes. Perfect served warm, they make a simple homemade treat that is both satisfying and versatile.
Ingredients: 250g Flour; Pinch of Salt; 3tsp Extra Virgin Oil; 1 Egg; 50g Brown Sugar; 300ml Milk (soya / oat)
Variations: Poppy Seed; Rasins; Vanila; Nuts; Grated Apple
Instructions: Mix Brown Sugar, Pinch of Salt and Flour and then add the Egg and Milk. Whisk together until smooth and add the Oil into the mix. Separate the batter into different bowls and add the variations accordingly. Depending on the variations you will want to add the brown sugar to suit the sweetness of the variation. Cook on low heat in pan until golden brown.

Title: Apple Pie (Hungarian)
Description: Apple Pie (Hungarian) is a comforting, home-baked dessert made with layers of buttery pastry and a soft, cinnamon-spiced apple filling. The shredded apples become tender and fragrant as they bake, while the golden crust adds a delicate crumble and sweetness to every bite. Warm, cosy, and full of classic flavour, it is a beautiful dessert to serve on its own or with a dusting of icing sugar.
Ingredients: 300g Flour; Pinch of Salt; 120g Butter; ½ Lemon Zest; 50g Powdered Sugar; 6 Medium Apples (Peeled and Shredded); 6g Baking Powder; 1 tsp Cinnamon; 5g Vanilla Essence; 4 tbs Ground Walnut; 2 Eggs (1 for brushing)
Instructions: Mix the Flour and Butter until crumbly then add the Egg, Powdered Sugar and Lemon Zest. Knead together. Divide the dough into two balls and allow to rest for 20 minutes. Peels the Apples and core and shred into a mixing bowl. Now add the Sugar, Cinnamon to the bowl and mix well.

Title: Caramelised Onions
Description: Rich, sweet, and deeply savoury, cooked slowly until soft, golden, and full of flavour. The natural sweetness of the onions develops as they gently soften, while the balsamic vinegar adds a slight tang and depth that makes them beautifully balanced. Perfect as a topping, side, or addition to many dishes, they bring warmth and richness to every bite.
Ingredients: 2 tbsp Olive Oil; 3 Large Onions (red or white); Pinch of Salt; 2 tbsp Soft Brown Sugar; 2 tbsp Balsamic Vinegar; Water
Instructions: Heat the oil in a pan over a low heat, add the onions along with a pinch of salt. Stir occasionally to prevent it sticking to the pan, add Water as necessary. Slow cook for 30-40 minutes until soft and golden brown. Once soft and golden brown, add the Brown Sugar and Balsamic Vinegar and cook for a further 5 minutes then serve.

Title: Granola Bar
Description: Chewy, lightly sweet, and packed with wholesome flavour, combining oats, dates, seeds, and nuts into a satisfying homemade snack. The natural sweetness of the fruit and syrup brings everything together, while the toasted ingredients add texture and a delicious nutty crunch. Perfect for breakfast on the go, lunchboxes, or an afternoon energy boost, they are a simple and versatile treat that can be adapted with your favourite mix-ins.
Ingredients: 150g Stoned Dates; 150G Porridge Oats; 100g Low Fat Spread; 4 tbsp. Agave Syrup; 50g Chopped Toasted Hazelnuts; 3 tbsp. Mixed Seeds; 50g Rasins
Instructions: Heat the oven to 170/190 degrees Celsius. And line backing tin with parchment. Blend Dates until smooth in food processor. Option 1) Use a saucepan and add the Dates, Low Fat Spread and Agave Syrup. Options 2) Add the Dates and Agave Syrup to a bowl. Add all the other ingredients and stir until mixed. Spoon mixture into a baking tin. Bake for 15-20 minutes, until golden brown.

Title: Pancakes (Quinoa)
Description: light, tender, and full of fresh flavour, combining cooked quinoa with lemon, vanilla, and blueberries for a wholesome twist on a classic treat. The quinoa adds a soft texture and gentle nuttiness, while the lemon brings brightness and the blueberries add bursts of natural sweetness. Delicious served warm, they make a nourishing dessert or sweet breakfast that feels both comforting and refreshing.
Ingredients: 1 Cup of Cooked and Cooled Quinoa; 1/3 Cup of Fresh Lemon Juice; ¾ Cup of Flour; Zest of 1 Lemon; 2 tsp. Baking Powder; ¼ Cup of Unsweetened soya or oat milk; ¼ tsp. Salt; 1 tsp. Vanilla Extract; 2 tbsp. Sugar or Honey; 1 tbsp. Olive Oil; 1 Egg; ¾ Cup of Fresh/Frozen Blueberries
Instructions: Whisk together the Quinao, Flour, Baking Powder and Salt. In a separate bowl, whisk together the Egg, Lemon Juice, Egg, Milk, Honey, Vanilla and Olive Oil. Combine in Ingredients and gently fold in the blueberries. If too thick add more milk. Then cook until golden brown.

Title: Mince Pies – Mince (part 1)
Description: Warm, fragrant filling made with softened apples, dried fruit, almonds, and festive spices, gently simmered until rich, sweet, and full of flavour. The fruit becomes soft and glossy, while the cinnamon, mixed spice, and cloves create a classic Christmas aroma with every spoonful. Finished with a splash of brandy if desired, it makes a comforting and traditional filling that brings warmth and richness to every mince pie.
Ingredients: 2 Apples; 3 tbsp. Brandy (optional); 400g Dried Fruit; 50g Almonds (sliced); 1 tsp. Mixed Spice; 2 tsp. Cinnamon; 1/8 tsp. Ground Cloves
Instructions: Wash, Core and chop the Apples and place into a medium pan, add the other Mince ingredients and bring to the boil and then reduce the heat and simmer for 15 minutes. Make sure the apple is mushy. Leave the Mince to cool and work on the dough (see part 2).

Title: Mince Pies – Dough (part 2)
Description: Soft, crumbly, and lightly sweet, creating a tender case that bakes to a delicate golden finish. The flour and sugar give it a classic sweet pastry texture, while the pecan nut butter adds richness and a subtle nutty flavour that makes it especially comforting. Easy to shape and perfect for holding a spiced fruit filling, it creates a beautifully crisp and flavourful base for homemade mince pies.
Ingredients: 125g Flour; 2 tbsp. Sugar; 5 tbsp. Pecan Nut Butter
Instructions: Sift the Flour and add salt into a bowl, stir in the Sugar and add the Pecan Nut Butter and lightly rub in with your finger tips, until it's incorporated and has a breadcrumb texture. Pour 4.5 table spoons of water and bring together with your hands to form a soft dough and add additional water if required. Knead gently to make sure everything is well combined and place in the fridge for 30 minutes. Pre-head the over to 180C. Roll the dough out onto a sheet of greaseproof paper and cut out circles to fit the cake holders. Place the circles into the cake holders and fill with the mince. Add some pastry lids for various designs or just circles, make sure there is a hole on top for the steam to escape. Bake in the oven for 15 minutes and turn the tray around and bake for another 5 minutes.

Title: Carrot & Coriander Soup
Description: This soup is smooth, warming, and full of fresh flavour, blending sweet carrots with fragrant coriander for a light yet comforting starter. The onions and potato give the soup a soft, velvety texture, while the coriander adds a gentle warmth and herby freshness that brightens every spoonful. Simple, nourishing, and easy to enjoy, it is a wholesome soup that is perfect served hot on a chilly day.
Ingredients: 1 tbsp. Vegetable Oil; Handful of Coriander; 1 Onion, chopped; 1 tsp. Ground Coriander; 1 potato, chopped; 450g carrots, peeled and chopped; 1.2L vegetable or chicken stock
Instructions: Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a large pan, add 1 chopped onion, then fry for 5 mins until softened. Stir in 1 tsp ground coriander and 1 chopped potato, then cook for 1 min. Add the 450g peeled and chopped carrots and 1.2l vegetable or chicken stock, bring to the boil, then reduce the heat. Cover and cook for 20 mins until the carrots are tender. Tip into a food processor with a handful of coriander then blitz until smooth. Return to pan, taste, add salt if necessary, then reheat to serve.

Title: Moroccan Couscous (part 1) - Roasted Vegetables
Description: A vibrant, fragrant dish filled with warm spices, roasted vegetables, and bursts of fresh flavour. The fluffy couscous is infused with cumin, coriander, cinnamon, and turmeric, while chickpeas, herbs, raisins, and pomegranate add sweetness, texture, and colour to every bite. Finished with crunchy almonds and fresh herbs, it is a wholesome and beautifully balanced main that feels both comforting and refreshing.
Ingredients: 2 tbsp. Extra Virgin Olive Oil; ½ Red Pepper, cut into small chunks; ½ Red Onion, cut into small chunks; 1 Courgette, cut into small chunks; Salt; 1 cup Grated Carrot; 400g Can Chickpeas (drain & rinsed); ½ cup Pomegranate Seeds; ½ cup fresh Coriander, chopped; ½ cup of fresh Mint; ½ cup fresh Parsley; ½ cup Toasted Flaked Almonds
Instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C fan. Scatter the red pepper, red onion, and courgette on a baking tray. Drizzle with the olive oil, sprinkle with salt, and bake for 20 minutes until tender and lightly roasted.

Title: Moroccan Couscous (part 2) - Couscous
Description: A vibrant, fragrant dish filled with warm spices, roasted vegetables, and bursts of fresh flavour. The fluffy couscous is infused with cumin, coriander, cinnamon, and turmeric, while chickpeas, herbs, raisins, and pomegranate add sweetness, texture, and colour to every bite. Finished with crunchy almonds and fresh herbs, it is a wholesome and beautifully balanced main that feels both comforting and refreshing.
Ingredients: 2 tbsp. Extra Virgin Olive Oil; 1 cup Grated Carrot; ½ Red Pepper, cut into small chunks; 400g Can Chickpeas (drain & rinsed); ½ Red Onion, cut into small chunks; ½ cup Pomegranate Seeds; 1 Courgette, cut into small chunks; ½ cup fresh Coriander, chopped; Salt
Instructions: In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the cumin, coriander, cinnamon, turmeric, black pepper, grated garlic, lemon juice, and olive oil with the boiling water. Stir through the dried couscous and raisins. Cover with cling film and leave to stand for 10 minutes. Once soaked and cooled slightly, fluff up the grains with a fork. Drain the chickpeas and add them to the bowl along with the grated carrot and chopped fresh herbs, reserving some herbs for the top. Stir everything together, then scatter over the almonds, pomegranate, and remaining herbs before serving.

Title: Risotto
Description: Rich, creamy, and deeply comforting, with tender rice slowly cooked until soft and full of savoury flavour. The shallots, garlic, thyme, and mushrooms create a warm and earthy base, while the gradual addition of stock gives the dish its smooth, velvety texture. Finished with a splash of milk for extra creaminess and adaptable with vegetables such as courgette, butternut squash, or spinach, it is a satisfying main that feels both hearty and elegant.
Ingredients: 2 Shallots / 1 Onion; Milk; 2/3 Garlic Cloves; Thyme; Rice; Vegetable Stock; Chestnut Mushrooms
Instructions: Cook of the Shallots / Onions in a pan. Prepare boiling water and Vegetable Stock In a measuring jug. Add the Garlic to the pan, add the Mushrooms and add the Thyme. Once the Mushrooms are cooked off, add the Rice. Cook over a medium heat, adding the Vegetable Stock bit by bit until the Rice absorbs. Add the variations and add Milk to make creamy as required. Butternut squash will need longer cooking so add that early.

Title: Chilli Con Carne
Description: A hearty, warming dish packed with rich tomato flavour, tender beans, and gently spiced peppers, onions, and garlic. The roasted peppers add a deep sweetness, while the spice mix brings warmth and depth to the savoury mince or soya base. Served with rice and filled with colourful vegetables, it is a comforting and satisfying main that is full of bold, homely flavour.
Ingredients: 2/3 Red Peppers; Kidney Beans; 1 Onion; Rice; 2 Garlic Cloves; Mince Meat / Soya Meat; Spice Mix; Extra Virgin Olive Oil; Sweetcorn; Chopped Tomatoes; Green Beans
Instructions: Cut the Peppers in half and take out the core and roast them in the oven. Once ready blend them in the blender. Caramelise the Onion and add Garlic, add Mince Meat / Soya Meat (separate pan). Fry until cooked. Add the blended Pepper sauce to one pan and add Chopped Tomatoes to the other. Add Mixed Spice to each pan. Add Vegetables to each pan. Cook the Rice separately in a pan. Simmer and serve. If doing the alternative with Butternut Squash, peel and roughly chop then bake until soft and then blend.

Title: Pancakes (Keto)
Description: Soft, fluffy, and gently sweet, offering a satisfying low-carb alternative to a classic favourite. Made with almond flour and vanilla, they have a light, tender texture with a delicate nuttiness that pairs beautifully with your favourite toppings. Served warm and golden from the pan, they make a comforting breakfast or dessert that feels both wholesome and indulgent.
Ingredients: 4 Large Eggs; ¾ cup unsweetened Almond Milk; ½ cup oil or butter; 2 ½ cups of almond flour; 2 tsp. vanilla extract; 2 tsp. baking powder; ¼ tsp. salt; ¼ cup Sweetener
Instructions: Blend the eggs, almond milk, oil, and vanilla extract until smooth and well combined. Add the almond flour, sweetener, baking powder, and salt, then blend again until the batter is smooth. Leave the batter to rest for 5 minutes so that it thickens slightly. Meanwhile, heat a lightly oiled pan over a medium heat. Spoon small portions of batter into the pan, using around 3 tablespoons for each pancake. Cook until bubbles begin to appear on the surface and the edges look set, then carefully turn with a thin spatula. Cook until golden brown on both sides, then remove from the pan. For the best texture, place the cooked pancakes on a wire rack while you finish the rest of the batch.

Title: Omelette
Description: Light, fluffy, and endlessly adaptable, this omelette folds softly cooked eggs around a warm, savoury filling. The gentle heat keeps the eggs tender while the cheese melts into every fold, making it a quick and satisfying way to start the day. Simple, protein-rich, and easy to dress up with vegetables or herbs, it is a reliable low-carb breakfast staple.
Ingredients: 3 Large Eggs; Pinch of Salt; Black Pepper; 1 tbsp. Butter or Olive Oil; 30g Grated Cheddar Cheese; Handful of Chopped Spinach or Mushrooms (optional)
Instructions: Crack the Eggs into a bowl, season with Salt and Pepper, and whisk until smooth. Heat the Butter or Oil in a non-stick pan over a medium heat. Pour in the Eggs and swirl to cover the base of the pan. As the edges begin to set, gently push them towards the centre with a spatula, tilting the pan so the uncooked egg runs to the edges. Scatter the Cheese and any Vegetables over one half once the top is nearly set. Fold the omelette in half and cook for a further minute until the cheese melts. Slide onto a plate and serve immediately.

Title: Scrambled Eggs with Avocado
Description: Creamy scrambled eggs paired with cool, buttery avocado for a breakfast that is both comforting and nourishing. The eggs are cooked low and slow for a soft, silky texture, while the avocado adds a rich contrast that keeps the dish satisfying without any need for toast. A simple, steady way to start the day without spiking blood sugar.
Ingredients: 3 Large Eggs; 1 tbsp. Butter; Pinch of Salt; Black Pepper; 1 Ripe Avocado; Squeeze of Lemon Juice; Chilli Flakes (optional)
Variations: Smoked Salmon; Cherry Tomatoes; Fresh Chives
Instructions: Crack the Eggs into a bowl with a pinch of Salt and whisk lightly. Melt the Butter in a non-stick pan over a low heat. Pour in the Eggs and stir gently and continuously with a spatula, keeping the heat low so the eggs cook slowly into soft, creamy curds. Remove from the heat just before fully set, as they will continue cooking in the residual warmth. While the eggs cook, halve the Avocado, remove the stone, and slice or mash the flesh, then squeeze over a little Lemon Juice to stop it browning. Serve the Eggs alongside or over the Avocado, finished with Black Pepper and Chilli Flakes if using.

Title: Chicken Caesar Salad
Description: A crisp, refreshing salad built around tender chicken and crunchy lettuce, tossed in a rich, garlicky dressing. The Parmesan adds a salty depth while the dressing coats every leaf, making it a filling and satisfying lunch without any need for croutons or bread. Cool, crisp, and full of flavour, it is an easy low-carb option any day of the week.
Ingredients: 2 Chicken Breasts; 1 tbsp. Olive Oil; Salt; Black Pepper; 1 Large Romaine Lettuce, chopped; 40g Parmesan, shaved; 4 tbsp. Mayonnaise; 1 Garlic Clove, crushed; 1 tsp. Dijon Mustard; 1 tsp. Lemon Juice; 1 tsp. Worcestershire Sauce; 1 Anchovy Fillet, finely chopped (optional)
Instructions: Season the Chicken Breasts with Salt and Pepper and rub with a little Olive Oil. Heat a pan over a medium-high heat and cook the Chicken for 6-7 minutes on each side until golden and cooked through. Set aside to rest for a few minutes before slicing. Meanwhile, make the dressing by whisking together the Mayonnaise, crushed Garlic, Dijon Mustard, Lemon Juice, Worcestershire Sauce and Anchovy if using, until smooth. Toss the chopped Lettuce with the dressing until well coated. Top with the sliced Chicken and shaved Parmesan, then finish with a crack of Black Pepper.

Title: Ham Cheese Salad Plate
Description: A simple, no-cook plate of sliced ham, cheese, and crisp fresh vegetables, perfect for a quick and satisfying lunch. The saltiness of the ham and cheese pairs well with the crunch of fresh salad, making it an easy, balanced option that needs no cooking at all. Light, refreshing, and endlessly customisable, it is an ideal grab-and-go low-carb lunch.
Ingredients: 120g Sliced Ham; 100g Sliced Cheese (Cheddar or Swiss); Mixed Salad Leaves; ½ Cucumber, sliced; 1 Tomato, sliced; ¼ Red Onion, thinly sliced; 1 tbsp. Olive Oil; Splash of Vinegar; Salt; Black Pepper
Instructions: Arrange the Salad Leaves over a plate as a base. Lay the sliced Ham and Cheese over the top, either folded or rolled for presentation. Scatter over the sliced Cucumber, Tomato, and Red Onion. Drizzle with Olive Oil and a splash of Vinegar, then season with Salt and Black Pepper. Serve chilled straight away.

Title: Chicken Lettuce Wraps
Description: Juicy, well-seasoned chicken mince wrapped in crisp, cool lettuce leaves for a light and hands-on lunch. The savoury filling is packed with flavour from garlic, ginger, and soy, while the lettuce keeps everything fresh and crunchy in place of a heavier wrap or bun. A fun, satisfying way to enjoy a low-carb meal.
Ingredients: 500g Chicken Mince; 1 tbsp. Olive Oil; 1 Garlic Clove, crushed; 1 tsp. Grated Ginger; 3 tbsp. Soy Sauce; 1 tbsp. Rice Vinegar; ½ Red Pepper, finely diced; 4 Spring Onions, sliced; 1 Large Lettuce (Iceberg or Little Gem), leaves separated
Instructions: Heat the Olive Oil in a large pan or wok over a medium-high heat. Add the Chicken Mince and cook, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned and cooked through. Add the crushed Garlic and grated Ginger and cook for a further minute until fragrant. Stir in the Soy Sauce, Rice Vinegar, diced Red Pepper, and most of the Spring Onions, then cook for 3-4 minutes until the vegetables soften slightly. Remove from the heat. Spoon the warm chicken mixture into the separated Lettuce leaves, scatter with the remaining Spring Onions, and serve immediately while the lettuce is still crisp.

Title: Pork Loin with Vegetables
Description: Tender, juicy pork loin roasted alongside a colourful mix of vegetables for a wholesome and satisfying dinner. The pork stays succulent as it cooks, while the vegetables soften and caramelise gently in the oven, soaking up all the savoury juices. A comforting, balanced main that needs little more than a squeeze of lemon to finish.
Ingredients: 600g Pork Loin; 2 tbsp. Olive Oil; Salt; Black Pepper; 1 tsp. Dried Thyme; 2 Courgettes, sliced; 1 Red Pepper, chunked; 1 Red Onion, chunked; 200g Broccoli Florets; 2 Garlic Cloves, crushed
Instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C fan. Rub the Pork Loin with 1 tablespoon of the Olive Oil, Salt, Black Pepper, and Dried Thyme. Place in a roasting tin and roast for 25-30 minutes, or until cooked through with an internal temperature of 70°C, then rest for 5 minutes before slicing. While the pork roasts, toss the Courgettes, Red Pepper, Red Onion, and Broccoli with the remaining Olive Oil, crushed Garlic, and a little Salt. Spread over a separate baking tray and roast for 20-25 minutes alongside the pork, turning halfway, until tender and lightly golden. Serve the sliced Pork Loin with the roasted vegetables.

Title: Beef Burger (No Bun) with Salad and Coleslaw
Description: A juicy, well-seasoned beef patty served open with crisp salad and creamy coleslaw in place of a bun. The beef stays tender and full of flavour, while the fresh salad and tangy coleslaw add crunch and balance without any need for bread. A satisfying, hearty dinner that still feels like a proper burger.
Ingredients: 400g Beef Mince; 1 Garlic Clove, crushed; ½ tsp. Smoked Paprika; Salt; Black Pepper; 1 tbsp. Olive Oil; Mixed Salad Leaves; 1 Tomato, sliced; ¼ Red Onion, sliced; 200g White Cabbage, shredded; 1 Carrot, grated; 3 tbsp. Mayonnaise; 1 tsp. Vinegar
Instructions: In a bowl, mix the Beef Mince with the crushed Garlic, Smoked Paprika, Salt, and Black Pepper. Shape into two patties. Heat the Olive Oil in a pan over a medium-high heat and cook the patties for 4-5 minutes on each side until cooked through and well browned. For the coleslaw, mix the shredded Cabbage and grated Carrot with the Mayonnaise and Vinegar, seasoning to taste. Arrange the Salad Leaves, sliced Tomato, and Red Onion on a plate, top with the cooked Beef Patty, and serve with a generous spoonful of the coleslaw on the side.

Title: Chicken Curry (Low Carb)
Description: A warming, aromatic curry made with tender chicken simmered in a rich tomato and coconut sauce, spiced with ginger, garlic, and curry spices. The sauce becomes thick and fragrant as it cooks, clinging to every piece of chicken, while cauliflower rice keeps the whole dish comforting without the carbs of traditional rice. A cosy, flavour-packed dinner that is easy to make in one pan.
Ingredients: 2 Chicken Breasts, diced; 1 tbsp. Olive Oil; 1 Onion, chopped; 2 Garlic Cloves, crushed; 1 tsp. Grated Ginger; 2 tsp. Curry Powder; ½ tsp. Turmeric; 400g Chopped Tomatoes; 200ml Coconut Milk; Salt; Fresh Coriander; 1 Head Cauliflower, riced
Instructions: Heat the Olive Oil in a large pan over a medium heat and fry the chopped Onion for 5 minutes until softened. Add the crushed Garlic and grated Ginger and cook for a further minute. Stir in the Curry Powder and Turmeric and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the diced Chicken and cook for 2-3 minutes until lightly sealed on the outside. Pour in the Chopped Tomatoes and Coconut Milk, season with Salt, and bring to a simmer. Cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce has thickened. Meanwhile, steam or microwave the Cauliflower Rice for 4-5 minutes until tender. Serve the Curry over the Cauliflower Rice, finished with fresh Coriander.

Title: Meatballs with Tomato Sauce
Description: Tender, well-seasoned meatballs gently simmered in a rich, herby tomato sauce until soft and full of flavour. The meatballs stay juicy as they cook through in the sauce, while the tomato base thickens and deepens in flavour the longer it simmers. A comforting, classic dinner that pairs well with a simple green vegetable or courgette noodles.
Ingredients: 400g Beef or Pork Mince; 1 Egg; 30g Grated Parmesan; 1 Garlic Clove, crushed; Salt; Black Pepper; 1 tbsp. Olive Oil; 1 Onion, finely chopped; 400g Chopped Tomatoes; 1 tsp. Dried Oregano; Fresh Basil
Instructions: In a bowl, combine the Mince, Egg, Parmesan, half the crushed Garlic, Salt, and Black Pepper. Mix well and shape into small meatballs. Heat the Olive Oil in a large pan over a medium heat and brown the meatballs on all sides, then remove and set aside. In the same pan, fry the chopped Onion for 5 minutes until softened, then add the remaining Garlic and cook for a further minute. Pour in the Chopped Tomatoes and Dried Oregano, season, and bring to a simmer. Return the meatballs to the pan, cover, and simmer gently for 15-20 minutes until the meatballs are cooked through and the sauce has thickened. Finish with torn fresh Basil before serving.

Title: Greek Yoghurt with Berries
Description: Thick, creamy Greek yoghurt topped with fresh, lightly sweet berries and a scattering of nuts for crunch. The tang of the yoghurt balances beautifully with the natural sweetness of the berries, making it a light, refreshing breakfast or snack that comes together in minutes. Simple, cooling, and steady on blood sugar, it is an easy everyday favourite.
Ingredients: 200g Full Fat Greek Yoghurt; 80g Mixed Berries (Blueberries, Raspberries, Strawberries); 1 tbsp. Chopped Almonds or Walnuts; Pinch of Cinnamon (optional)
Variations: Chia Seeds; Flaked Coconut; Drizzle of Honey (small amount)
Instructions: Spoon the Greek Yoghurt into a bowl or glass. Scatter over the Mixed Berries, either whole or roughly chopped depending on size. Top with the Chopped Nuts and a pinch of Cinnamon if using. Serve immediately while the berries are fresh.

Title: Almonds, Walnuts and Peanuts Snack
Description: A simple, crunchy mix of roasted nuts, perfect for keeping energy steady between meals. The combination of almonds, walnuts, and peanuts offers a satisfying contrast of textures and flavours, from buttery and rich to lightly toasted and nutty. Portable and easy to prepare in batches, it is a reliable low-carb snack for any time of day.
Ingredients: 50g Almonds; 50g Walnuts; 50g Peanuts; Pinch of Salt (optional); ½ tsp. Olive Oil (if roasting)
Instructions: If serving raw, simply combine the Almonds, Walnuts, and Peanuts in a bowl or portion into small containers for snacking. To roast, preheat the oven to 160°C fan, toss the nuts lightly in Olive Oil and a pinch of Salt, and spread over a baking tray. Roast for 8-10 minutes, shaking the tray halfway through, until lightly golden and fragrant. Allow to cool completely before storing in an airtight container.

Title: Boiled Eggs
Description: Simple, protein-packed boiled eggs with a perfectly set white and a yolk anywhere from soft to firm, depending on preference. A steady, no-fuss breakfast or snack that needs nothing more than a pinch of salt, boiled eggs are one of the easiest ways to start the day without affecting blood sugar. Easy to prepare in batches and keep on hand for the week.
Ingredients: 4 Large Eggs; Salt; Black Pepper
Variations: Soft Boiled; Hard Boiled; Sprinkle of Paprika
Instructions: Place the Eggs in a saucepan and cover with cold water. Bring to the boil over a high heat. Once boiling, reduce to a simmer. For soft-boiled eggs, cook for 6 minutes; for a jammy yolk, cook for 8 minutes; for fully hard-boiled eggs, cook for 10-11 minutes. Once cooked, transfer the Eggs immediately to a bowl of cold water to stop them cooking further and make peeling easier. Peel and season with Salt and Black Pepper before serving.
